descriptions.text: MAP Protocol's OmniService cross-chain messaging proxy exposed retryMessageIn, a function intended to re-process a previously failed inbound cross-chain message. However it did not properly verify that the supplied message had actually been received and validated by the relay/light-client before — it trusted the caller-supplied fromChain, orderId, from, and message payload. The attacker crafted a message payload encoding a token-mint instruction (recipient, amount, decimals) targeting the MAPO token and called retryMessageIn directly, causing the OmniService to execute the forged cross-chain message and mint 1,000,000,000,000,000 MAPO to the attacker. The root cause is insufficient validation of inbound message authenticity on the retry path, enabling arbitrary minting. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0x31e56b4737649e0acdb0ebb4eca44d16aeca25f60c022cbde85f092bde27664a Analysis: https://x.com/MapProtocol/status/2059587998409490510

MAP Protocol’s Butter Bridge V3.1 accepted a crafted retry-message path on Ethereum mainnet and minted 1,000,000,000,000,000 MAPO to an attacker-controlled address on 2026-05-20. Public records and secondary reporting also place the incident on BNB Chain, but only the Ethereum transaction is independently reproduced here. The bridge-side retry path accepted an unbacked MAPO mint. Public analyses attribute the trigger to weak message validation in retryMessageIn, likely involving packed-field hashing over dynamic data, but the historical victim source was not independently available, so the exact line-level defect remains unverified.
